Baby moose sort of appeared not far behind me and mommy moose was not far away. Baby moose was curious and kept getting closer and closer. So, I pet his nose and the top of his head, right around his ears. He seemed reasonably satisfied and mommy moose decided not to kill me, something I'm grateful for.

By the same token, we fairly frequently get tourists who go 'moose spotting.' They drive around looking to find moose. Sometimes, they get out of their car and approach a moose. Moose are usually nice enough to lumber away. Sometimes, moose is not in the mood to meander off and stomps the fuck out of a tourist. It isn't usually fatal, but there have been two such fatalities since I moved here. What's funny is the people that live through it get charged for molesting wildlife.

Under nearly all circumstances, touching (or attempting to do so) wild animals is against the law. My doing so with the baby moose was against the law, but I'd have won in court (probably) using what's known as an 'affirmative defense.' That basically means I committed the act, but did so for a justifiable reason - namely baby moose was approaching me and I had nowhere to retreat to. But, that's very different from hopping out of the car and walking over to pet the wild moose. That's not only dumb, it's illegal.
